Lei,

On May 31, 2007, at 6:13 PM, Lei Wu wrote:

> I'm trying to use JRI to replace my old code that uses Rserve now.
> I wonder how JRI handle the consecutive request. For example, after
> I issue a very time consuming R command through JRI, I issue second
> command through JRI right after this. Is there any way that JRI or
> JGR can remember the second command and execute it after the first
> one finished? Or I should write my own queue to save all command?
>

I'm not quite sure what you mean - if you try to send a request while
another one is processed, it will block until it is processed as
well, so it is a kind of implicit queuing that you get. Clearly, only
one eval will be inside R at each given time as R is not threaded
(unless you use multiple JVMs ...).

Cheers,
Simon

Sure. Actually, rtest.java does exactly that as-is (it just prints it  
to the console). All you really have to implement is rWriteConsole -  
it will be called whenever R prints something. You can make it to e- 
mail the intermediate result to your boss or whatever you like ;). If  
you have problems with that, please be more specific as you what your  
code does, because the rtest.java example actually does exactly what  
you describe.

You don't have to, but you can. Clearly, you could change  
rReadConsole such that it doesn't read from the stdin and add your  
queue instead if you want a true console. But there is no real  
difference in just using eval (because that's all the REPL does).

Cheers,

messages.subject_clean: EPS graphics and OpenOffice
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

EPS graphics made by JGR (JavaGD) can be included into LaTeX output, but when
I try to insert them into an OpenOffice Writer document I get the error
"Unknown graphic format". The result is the same if I do the following
commands directly in R:

  x <- 1:10
  postscript(file = "foo.eps", paper="special", width=6, height=4, horizontal=F)
  plot(x)
  dev.off()

I can add the eps picture to OpenOffice if I do the following:

  eps2eps foo.eps bar.eps

The script eps2eps is part gs-common package, but probably the definitive
solution would be the addition of the option "onefile=F" to the postscript
command:

  postscript(file = "foo.eps", onefile=F, paper="special", width=6, height=4, horizontal=F)

This option makes no difference for LaTeX, but now OpenOffice can read the eps
file. So, I suggest that the option "onefile" was changed from TRUE to FALSE
in toolkit/JavaGD.java file (at JGR source). In R postscript device,
"onefile" means "many pages in one file", and that's why it's better
that it is set to FALSE.

I'm using OpenOffice 2.2.0-1ubuntu3 (Ubuntu 7.04), R 2.5.0, JGR 1.17, JavaGD 0.4-2.

Best regards,

--
Jakson Aquino
http://JAlvesAq.googlepages.com
